Apology, Accountability: IIT Bombay Director Signs 18-Point Charter Amid Protests Over Student's Suicide

IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare has signed an 18‑point student charter after three days of protests demanding accountability over a student’s suicide, News18 India reports. The charter, presented by student representatives, includes an independent inquiry into the incident, mental‑health support enhancements, and stricter grievance‑redress mechanisms. It also calls for transparent communication from the administration and regular feedback sessions with the student body. The signing marks a rare concession for the institute’s leadership, which initially resisted the protesters’ demands. Student leaders welcomed the move but stressed that implementation must be monitored closely. The charter also proposes revisions to academic policies, including a review of grading practices and the introduction of peer‑support programmes. The director’s office has yet to release a detailed timeline for executing the points. The protests have highlighted ongoing concerns about student well‑being at one of India’s premier technical institutions. Observers say the charter could set a precedent for other universities facing similar crises.

What to watch: The government’s response to the charter and whether an independent probe will be instituted promptly.
